files.title: A · 直立平衡
files.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: character turnaround for an original mobile match-3 duck mascot, concept only.
Input images 1-3: actual competitor goose-and-prop models, reference ONLY for economical rounded toy surfaces and narrow integrated silhouette. Create an original DUCK, not the reference goose; do not include any props in this turnaround.
Create one clean horizontal landscape three-view sheet, three equal columns: exact front, exact left profile with bill pointing left, and front-left three-quarter. Show the SAME character, same proportions, equal full-body height, feet aligned on a single baseline. All views unoccluded, ample space between them, all body parts in frame. No text, lettering, arrows or dimensions.
Character: slender milk-white adult cartoon DUCK, small head, narrow elongated torso, modestly elongated neck with a real substantial cross-section. Overall height including feet about 2.6 times maximum torso width, small head width about 0.8 torso width. Lower belly pulled in, never a fat pear, never a large-headed baby duck. The body should slide into a narrow cup, toy shell or food sleeve. Two tiny plain black bead eyes, no large eyes, no white sclera, no eyelashes. Clearly broad FLAT orange duck bill with round spatulate tip, top and bottom close together, no pointed goose bill, no smile line or nostrils. Orange modest webbed feet with short legs, wings flush against torso, a short unobtrusive tail. Plain clean white colour fields, no clothes, no hair tuft, no accessory, no pink cheeks, no spots, no textures or feathers. Original simple affectionate slightly mischievous mascot.
Style: production-oriented low-detail smooth rounded 3D toy concept, soft satin plastic, broad gentle bevels, neutral white diffuse studio light, subtle shape shading, no chrome, no shiny ceramic glare, no fluffy feathers. Flat pale warm-gray background, subtle contact shadow only, no floor horizon. Front and profile should read like orthographic views; 3/4 also orthographic. Same lighting and same scale across future variants. White silhouette visibly distinct against gray.
Important: genuinely NARROW and long, not plump, not round belly; visually clean enough to reproduce within 2000-4000 triangles. Neck is medium length, not swan/goose length, not wire-thin.

Variant A, recommended balanced integration: an almost vertical neck with one very gentle forward curve, relatively straight slim torso, head held level, relaxed alert bead eyes, flat bill closed. A narrow upright silhouette with a mild friendly forward lean. The neck should be around one quarter of total standing height; keep a visible continuous transition from chest through neck.

files.title: B · 紧凑柔和
files.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: original mobile match-3 duck mascot VARIANT B turnaround concept.
Input image 1 is variant A, a reference for material, framing, precise three-column layout and palette. Produce a clearly different variant B of this same slender white duck design family, keeping the SAME camera scale, body height, neutral light gray backdrop, soft studio light and smooth satin toy rendering. All three views must depict the identical new B character: FRONT, LEFT PROFILE bill pointing left, FRONT-LEFT THREE-QUARTER. No text. Full bodies and feet visible, baseline aligned. Wide sheet with three equal columns.
CHANGES for B: a graceful but SHORTER gently S-curved medium neck, with head reaching forward a little more. Smooth flowing chest transition; SMALLER head, around 85% of reference head size. Broad closed orange flat spatulate DUCK bill 10% shorter than A and more flattened, never pointed. A relaxed subtly cheeky personality through head attitude, not facial decoration. The neck bend should be readable from side, less visible from front. Neck thickness remains strong enough for a small toy. Eyes tiny round black beads.
KEEP slender elongated narrow white torso, tucked belly, wings flush to body, small tail, short legs and orange webbed feet. Absolutely NO fat belly, NO big baby head, NO eyelashes, eyebrows, pink cheeks, plumage texture, hair, clothes or accessories. NOT swan, NOT a goose. The duck is intended to fit into narrow cups, toy shells and food casings.
Subtle rounded low-detail toy geometry suitable for low-poly model reproduction. One consistent same duck across all views, orthographic presentation, same crop and generous margins as A. Only a three-view sheet, no props, no additional images.

files.title: C · 向前探头
files.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Original match-3 duck mascot concept, VARIANT C: small head, alert forward lean.
Image 1 is variant A, a reference for palette, satin toy surface, scale and three-column presentation.
Generate a new three-view sheet in the same landscape aspect: front, left side profile with bill pointing left, front-left three-quarter. Same white duck design in all views, identical height and body width across views, full body, feet on baseline. No labels or text. Same gray backdrop and neutral soft lighting as A.
C must be visibly distinct: head is only TWO THIRDS as wide as the torso (about 25% smaller than A), bill very clearly broad orange flat spatulate duck bill, width just wider than head, tiny black bead eyes. Neck is medium-long and leans forward by about 20 degrees, then a small upward turn at head, creating a curious searching/probing gesture; the profile has visible negative space under the chin. Not a long swan neck. The slim elongated torso also leans forward slightly and is balanced by webbed feet. Tail points back slightly. Wings remain tightly folded. Keep head level with a mildly inquisitive face, no eyebrows.
NARROW torso and tucked belly, like a slender upright duck that fits into a narrow toy shell, no oversized belly or rear end. No fat baby duck, no clothes, no feathers or hair tuft, no logos, no extra props, no pink cheeks, no large white eyes, no pointed goose bill. Only fine, economical soft toy forms, no detail clutter. The difference versus A should be clear in side view and in the smaller head, without changing the core identity, body width or rendering style.

files.title: 蛋挞鸭 · 薄盘融合
files.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: single original 3D mobile match-3 duck-and-prop concept preview, not a finished mesh.
Image 1 is the APPROVED-FOR-EXPLORATION variant B duck turnaround: use exactly its narrow milk-white adult duck design, small bead eyes, rounded small head, relatively broad orange FLAT DUCK bill with spatulate tip, medium length slim neck, tucked slender torso and orange webbed feet. It is a design reference, not a collage to copy. Image 2 is the actual competitor goose-and-prop model: use only the way an object wraps and contains a bird, not its pointed bill or goose proportions.
Make a NEW unified duck-and-prop toy design. SINGLE entire object, centered, front-left three-quarter orthographic at about 25 degrees above, bill points towards viewer-left. Entire silhouette including feet must fit within 10% padding. Same pale neutral gray studio background, neutral white soft lighting, simple satin plastic toy-like rendering as the B duck reference. Clear economical rounded solid forms, no excessive details or photorealistic textures.
Critical assembly: the slender duck BODY is INSIDE and occupies the prop shell; the neck grows continuously out of a real opening, and the two small feet protrude below where appropriate. Wing tips may fit against shell, but never a second full duck perched on a prop. One duck, one coherent assembled collectible object. Keep duck neck thickness and broad flat orange bill recognizable at small screen size, use compact medium neck rather than extremely long exposed goose neck. Shell must hide belly and torso, not add a giant fat duck to the outside.
No text, no letters, no logos, no UI, no watermark, no scene or stand. No loose separated parts, no hovering neck, no transparent body, no second bird. No accessories that aren't part of the requested prop. No hair tuft, no clothes, no eyelashes or pink cheeks. Food/prop colour is distinct from white duck neck. All white duck body parts have the same white as B.

PROP: EGG TART DUCK, refined slender integration version. Very important: NOT an upright deep pastry bowl with a duck sitting inside. Use a SHALLOW circular egg tart disc, pastry depth only 18 percent of tart diameter, with broad yellow custard face and rounded scalloped golden crust edge. Hold the tart almost VERTICALLY, like a round shield or flat shell around the concealed duck torso, its custard face tilted toward camera; this preserves the competitor reference image 2's upright disc silhouette. The thin tart disc is the duck's external body shell.
A narrow white neck grows from one small neat opening near the UPPER RIGHT quadrant of the custard face, bends forward out of the surface and then UP, with the SAME B small head and broad orange FLAT duck bill. Head is only around ONE THIRD of tart diameter. Keep the exposed neck medium-short and compact, not a long swan neck. Side of head and bill face viewer-left. Two SMALL orange webbed feet appear just under the bottom edge, no long legs. White body entirely hidden in disc, tail/wing may barely peek from behind, not through crust randomly.
Keep whole assembly around 1.25 times as high as tart diameter. The custard face must remain visible as a shallow egg tart, not be obscured by the duck. Food surface is smooth simple toy satin, two golden crust colour bands and a few very BROAD toasted patches, NO photoreal flaky texture, no speckles, no shiny wet custard. All parts look manufacturable as low-detail rounded solid toy. Neck-to-tart opening must be a real connected continuous junction, no severed neck pasted on top. Main emphasis: thin shallow upright tart and SMALL head, economical silhouette, NO fat belly.

PROP: STEEL MUG DUCK. Keep the silhouette compact and longer than wide, about 1.5 width to height. The shell is a recognisable simple mug, satin LIGHT COOL GRAY with broad soft restrained highlights rather than mirror/chrome, ONE metal colour group, darker interior, rounded thick rim. No rust, rivets, words, seams, logos or separate stand. Do not overinflate head or belly. Camera is the same front-left above three-quarter product view as the other concepts, but freely rotate the assembled object to show open rim and head clearly. Neck and mug connections must read naturally.

Three-quarter camera slightly above shows both numeral face and neck connection; head does not obscure numeral. Simple satin toy material, broad colour areas, same gray background and soft neutral light as B and the other concepts. Compact piece, entire object and feet centered with generous margin.
